name: What is the difference between ceramic and porcelain tile for bathrooms?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between ceramic and porcelain tile for bathrooms?

acceptedAnswer.text: Porcelain tile is denser, more water-resistant, and harder to chip than standard ceramic, making it the preferred choice for high-moisture shower enclosures and bathroom floors. Ceramic tile is lighter and easier to cut, which can slightly reduce installation labor, but it absorbs moisture more readily if top glazes crack. Natural stone offers unique aesthetics but requires periodic sealing to avoid staining and water etching. For long-term durability and minimal upkeep in wet zones, glazed porcelain provides the best balance of moisture resistance and strength.
acceptedAnswer.description: Porcelain is denser and less porous than ceramic, making it significantly more water-resistant and durable for bathroom floors and shower walls.
